#freepalestine🇵🇸❤️ #palistanegaza #rek #fyp #foryou The question of Palestine is one of the most complex and painful issues in modern world politics. The Palestinian cause is not merely a territorial dispute — it touches on questions of justice, human rights, and national self-determination. The slogan "Free Palestine" has become a symbol of the Palestinian people's aspiration for freedom, dignity, and their own statehood. Understanding this issue requires examining its historical roots, the current humanitarian situation, the legal framework, and the arguments of all sides. Historical Context The modern history of Palestine begins with the collapse of the Ottoman Empire after World War I, when the territory came under British administration through a League of Nations mandate. In 1917, the Balfour Declaration expressed British support for a "national home for the Jewish people" in Palestine, while also stating that the rights of existing non-Jewish communities should not be prejudiced. In 1947, the United Nations adopted Resolution 181, proposing the partition of Palestine into separate Jewish and Arab states, with Jerusalem under international administration. The Jewish leadership accepted the plan; the Arab leadership rejected it. In 1948, the State of Israel was declared, triggering the first Arab-Israeli war. Around 700,000 Palestinians fled or were expelled — an event Palestinians call the Nakba, meaning "catastrophe."

Why is Gaza drowning? Images of floods engulfing Gaza have gone viral. Most coverage focuses on the humanitarian catastrophe. Few explain what caused it. Since October 2023, Israeli forces have destroyed nearly all of Gaza’s infrastructure. Up to 68 million tons of rubble now blanket the Strip. Homes, schools, hospitals, and basic services have been flattened, with at least 90 percent of the territory destroyed. Now, as winter sets in, the first rains are making what is left unlivable. At least five people have been killed after sand embankments collapsed in the downpour. None of this is new. The Israeli plan to make Gaza unlivable has been unfolding for years. In 2012, the UN warned that Gaza could be unlivable by 2020 because of repeated Israeli assaults, a crippling blockade, the collapse of its aquifer, energy shortages, and mass unemployment. Despite the so-called ceasefire, our reporter in Gaza describes a situation that is impossible to endure: no shelter, no aid, and a ban on rebuilding. Conditions are getting worse by the day.” @specter_affairs

Children in Gaza are being forced to trade their childhoods for survival as poverty, displacement and devastation from Israel’s war push families to the brink. Instead of attending school, many Palestinian children are selling food and water, collecting scrap metal, scavenging for firewood and working long hours to help feed their families. Some have become their households’ sole breadwinners after losing parents or other relatives. According to UNICEF, economic desperation has forced one in four families to resort to hazardous or exploitative child labor, with children as young as six taking on dangerous work. The crisis is deepening concerns about an entire generation growing up without education, stability or safety. Israel’s military offensive has devastated Gaza’s economy, destroyed schools and displaced hundreds of thousands of families, leaving children exposed to exploitation, malnutrition and severe psychological trauma. UNICEF estimates that around 60,000 children have lost one or both parents during the war and its aftermath. Aid organizations warn that without sustained humanitarian assistance, access to education and opportunities for families to earn a living, thousands more children could be pushed into work simply to survive.
